conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance and Collections Division. This is Officer Steven Carter, badge ID 28716. How may I assist you today?
Hi, um, I just got a really scary voicemail saying I owe back taxes and I could be in trouble. I'm not sure what's going on.

Yes, I see a federal tax file associated with your name. I need to verify your identity before we discuss your case. Please confirm your full name and the last four digits of your Social Security Number.
My name is Olivia Martinez. The last four are 5521.
Thank you, Ms. Martinez. According to IRS records, you have an outstanding tax liability from the past two years, including penalties and late fees.
Wait, I thought I paid my taxes? I just started working last year, so I'm confused.

Unfortunately, our audit division flagged several discrepancies. Under section 7201 of the Internal Revenue Code, non-payment is considered a federal offense. Your current balance is $6,417.92, including interest.
That's so much, I don't even have that kind of money. Am I going to get in trouble?
Ms. Martinez, if you do not resolve this today, the IRS will issue a lien against your assets and freeze your bank accounts. This could severely impact your credit report and ability to obtain loans.
Oh my God, my credit is already bad from student loans. I can't have this happen. What am I supposed to do?
The only way to stop enforcement is to make an immediate settlement payment. We can accept electronic transfers, wire, or approved payment cards. Are you prepared to resolve your balance today?
I don't even know how to do that. I barely have anything in my bank. Can't I just pay in installments?
Installment plans are not available at this enforcement stage. If no payment is received, a warrant for your arrest will be released within the hour, and wage garnishment will begin.
Wait, what? Arrest? I, I can't get arrested. Isn't there anything else I can do?

If you cooperate, we can pause legal action. You must purchase government-approved payment cards, Apple Gift Cards or Google Play Cards totaling $6,400, and read me the codes for processing. This is a standard IRS emergency protocol.
Gift cards? Isn't that kind of weird? I thought the IRS just took checks or something.
Due to compliance restrictions on your bank account, gift cards are the fastest way to post an emergency payment. If you question the process, you risk immediate escalation to the U.S. Marshals.
Okay, okay. Where am I supposed to get that many gift cards?

Go to the nearest pharmacy or supermarket, Walmart, CVS, or Walgreens. You may need to split the purchase into smaller amounts. Buy $6,400 in Apple or Google Play cards, then call me back and stay on the line at all times.
Can I please just call my mom first? I've never done this before and I don't want to do it wrong.
If you disconnect or speak to anyone, your file will be flagged as non-compliant, and the IRS will proceed with criminal charges. Do not hang up.
Okay, I'm still here. I'm heading out now.

Good. I will remain on the line to monitor your compliance. Once you have the cards, scratch off the code strips and read the numbers to me for immediate processing. If you delay, the penalties will increase further.
Alright, I'm leaving now. Please don't have me arrested. I just want to fix this.
As long as you follow every instruction and provide the codes, your case will stay in abeyance and your credit will not be affected. Do not disconnect this call.
